name: Post-structural feminism
summary: Post-structural feminism applies post-structuralist thought (Derrida, Lacan, Foucault) to gender, treating identities, including sex and the category of 'women', as contingent products of language, discourse and power rather than natural facts. It criticises phallocentric systems of meaning, rejects female essentialism, and favours provisional coalitions over a fixed feminist subject. It is chiefly a theoretical framework, so its economic and institutional positions are mostly inferred.
scope: The Anglo-American and French post-structural strand centred on Judith Butler (Gender Trouble) with the French theorists Cixous, Irigaray and Kristeva as precursors. It excludes materialist, radical and liberal feminisms that treat 'women' as a stable political class. Positions on economics, the state and foreign policy are mostly inferred from Butler's wider political writing.

keyFigures.name: Judith Butler
keyFigures.role: Author of Gender Trouble, the central statement of gender performativity

keyFigures.name: Luce Irigaray
keyFigures.role: French theorist who critiqued phallocentric psychoanalysis and sought a symbolic order for sexual difference

keyFigures.name: Hélène Cixous
keyFigures.role: Developer of écriture féminine, writing that disrupts patriarchal discourse

sources.title: Judith Butler
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.usedFor: Butler's wider politics: hate speech, censorship, state of exception, nonviolence, Occupy, trans rights, Israel.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Not a post-structural topic; inferred from Butler's support for social equality and economic justice (Occupy) and concern for precarious, unequally protected lives.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Inferred from Butler's backing of economic-justice demands; the sources give no wage doctrine.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Inferred: Butler's Occupy-era critique of profiteering and precarity points away from faith in markets, though the sources never address allocation.

public-ownership.rationale: Adherents are drawn to left politics but also distrust state power; nothing in the sources decides ownership questions.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Inferred from Butler's argument that those who profit from recession should redistribute wealth.

unions-good.rationale: Inferred from left-leaning solidarity and critique of precarity; unions are not discussed in the feminist-theory sources.

property-fundamental.rationale: Inferred: concern with precarity and dispossession cuts against treating property as an overriding right.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Inferred from Butler's support for economic justice against profiteering; no direct statement.

cut-welfare.rationale: Inferred from emphasis on interdependence and vulnerability that makes some lives unprotected.

worker-ownership.rationale: Left sympathies, but the theory itself does not take a position on workplace ownership.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Inferred from Foucault-derived suspicion of disciplinary power and from Butler's critique of the state of exception at Guantanamo.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Inferred from anti-normalizing, anti-disciplinary orientation; drugs are not discussed in the sources.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Butler's Excitable Speech holds that state-defined hate-speech law is hard to justify and criticizes state censorship of the MacKinnon type, so adherents are wary of legal restriction.

strong-leader.rationale: Inferred from distrust of concentrated authority and Butler's emphasis on assembly and plural, performative popular power.

state-harmful.rationale: Butler criticizes state sovereignty and exception, yet also appeals to legal protection; skeptical but not anti-state.

limit-guns.rationale: Inferred from Butler's nonviolence ethic and concern with vulnerability; guns are not discussed.

empower-police-military.rationale: Inferred from Butler's critique of state violence and the state of exception and her nonviolence stance.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Butler opposes state censorship of sexual expression (critique of MacKinnon); sex work itself is not stated, so inferred.

decide-locally.rationale: Butler favours provisional coalitions and rejects universal frameworks, but the sources say nothing about devolution.

rehabilitation.rationale: Inferred from Foucault-influenced critique of punishment and normalization; not stated in the feminist-theory sources.

traditional-family.rationale: Butler's argument that gender norms and heteronormativity are produced and policed makes the 'natural' traditional family a target of critique.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Butler writes on gay marriage but the source states no position; inferred support for legal equality alongside critique of marriage as a norm.

abortion-legal.rationale: Inferred from the feminist commitment to bodily autonomy; the sources do not discuss abortion directly, so the answer rests on shared feminist principles.

more-religion-public.rationale: Inferred from the rejection of universal foundations and from queer-feminist skepticism of religious norms.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Butler stresses that gender intersects with race, class and ethnicity and that exclusions follow from the default white feminist subject.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Gender Trouble treats gender as performative and discursively produced, and the Wikipedia overview stresses the social construction of gendered subjectivity.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Inferred from anti-essentialism about identity and wariness of exclusions made in the name of unity.

gradual-change.rationale: Butler advocates subversive repetition and disruption of norms, so adherents favour troubling institutions rather than deferring to them.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Inferred from Butler's attention to precarious, ungrievable lives and anti-exclusion stance.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Butler criticizes Geneva protections tied to recognized states but nothing in the sources endorses stronger international bodies.

free-trade.rationale: Inferred from critique of profiteering and precarity; trade is not discussed.

nation-first.rationale: Inferred from rejection of exclusionary unity and Butler's criticism of nationalist sovereignty.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Butler's critique of the state of exception and her nonviolence stance make adherents cautious about military force, though human-rights concern pulls the other way.

open-borders.rationale: Inferred from concern for precarious populations and anti-exclusion politics; not explicitly stated.

limit-growth.rationale: Nothing in the sources links this theory to degrowth or its opposite.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Inferred from left sympathies and interdependence themes; climate is not discussed in the sources.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Inferred from wariness of claims of neutral truth and progress.

expand-nuclear.rationale: No source or principle decides the issue.

revolution-justified.rationale: Butler favours subversive repetition and nonviolence as ethics, so adherents are split on revolution.

experts-over-public.rationale: The SEP notes continental feminists suspect truth claims mask power, undercutting expert authority as neutral.

central-planning.rationale: Inferred from suspicion of totalizing frameworks and universal blueprints.

socialized-markets.rationale: Left sympathies but no stated view on market socialism.

land-value-tax.rationale: Not a concern of the theory.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Inferred from Butler's redistribution argument; inheritance itself is not discussed.

basic-income.rationale: Inferred from Butler's support for equality and attention to precarity; not stated.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: The theory has no position on trade protection.

state-directs-investment.rationale: No stated position; suspicion of state power balanced by left sympathies.

widespread-small-property.rationale: The sources do not address ownership structure.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: The sources do not address abolition of wage labour; adherents are mostly not class-abolitionist theorists.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Inferred: a market-money position is far from the left egalitarianism Butler supports.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Inferred from distrust of state-recognised bodies and fixed categories.

one-party-rule.rationale: Butler rejects a guiding ideology that presumes unity in advance and favours open, coalitional politics.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Inferred from rejection of hereditary, naturalised hierarchy.

democracy-best.rationale: Butler's emphasis on assembly and plural popular power suggests support, but the theory also critiques the exclusions of liberal democratic subjects.

direct-votes.rationale: Assembly and participation are valued, but no stance on referendums is stated.

workers-councils.rationale: The theory is not about institutional design; adherents are split.

right-to-secede.rationale: The sources say nothing on secession; Butler's criticism of nationalism and of exclusionary states leaves adherents split.

natural-rulers.rationale: Anti-essentialism denies that fixed natural categories justify hierarchy; Butler treats such naturalisation as produced by power.

political-violence-never.rationale: Butler defends nonviolence as an ethical position within politics, though not absolute pacifism for all adherents.

war-builds-character.rationale: Inferred from Butler's nonviolence ethic and critique of state violence.

separate-church-state.rationale: Inferred from rejection of religiously grounded norms; not stated.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Inferred from the view that foundational, naturalised norms are products of power.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Inferred from left egalitarianism and critique of unequal protection.

military-superiority.rationale: Inferred from Butler's critique of state violence and sovereign exception.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Butler's critique of unity and exclusion built on a single category applies directly to ethnic foundations of identity.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Foucauldian history is not class-driven; Butler supports economic justice, but adherents are split on Marxist history.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Anti-essentialism and equality commitments pull in one direction, suspicion of fixed ideals in another; no stated view.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Inferred from the anti-colonial and anti-exclusion orientation; not stated.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Inferred from Butler's attention to differential grievability and to the Western bias of universal frameworks.

civilizational-union.rationale: Inferred from wariness of unified identities.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Butler stresses interdependence and shared vulnerability over self-sufficient self-interest.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Inferred: interdependence is valued, but subordinating individuals to community norms conflicts with critique of normalization.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Nature is not addressed; many adherents distrust appeals to the natural.

limit-population.rationale: Inferred from suspicion of state control of bodies and reproduction.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Post-structural feminism is a theory of gender and discourse, and the overview gives no view on industrialisation.

accelerate-technology.rationale: The overview gives no position on technological pace; adherents split between cyborg-friendly and critical views.

human-enhancement.rationale: Inferred from the view that the body is not a fixed nature and that identities are open to remaking.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Inferred from Foucault-influenced concern with technologies of power and claims of neutral knowledge.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Inferred from suspicion of surveillance as a form of power.

restore-past-order.rationale: Rejection of naturalised order and fixed identity makes restoring a past gender or social order contrary to the theory.

results-over-ideology.rationale: SEP notes continental feminists doubt neutral truth claims; 'results' standards are seen as value-laden.

direct-action.rationale: Butler analyses assembly and subversive public acts as forms of performative political power.

means-match-ends.rationale: Butler's nonviolence-as-ethic and prefigurative assembly suggest means embody ends; inferred.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Inferred only from distrust of appeals to a natural human condition; the sources never discuss primitivism.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Gender division of labour is criticized, but total abolition is not stated.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Inferred from vulnerability and interdependence emphasis.

production-for-use.rationale: Left sympathies but the sources give no economic doctrine.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Butler criticizes profiteering, but the specific Marxist exploitation claim is not hers.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Inferred from rejection of a pre-given collective subject and of dictatorial rule.

collective-farming.rationale: Agrarian organisation is outside the theory's scope and nothing can be inferred from its principles.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Butler criticises state violence and profiteering, but no source ties war to capitalism as a necessity.

taxation-theft.rationale: Directly opposed to the redistributive politics Butler endorses.

harm-principle.rationale: Butler favours expressive freedom but also treats speech and norms as capable of harm, so views are split.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Butler argues that the juridical subject before the law is produced by power and that identity groups are constituted rather than pre-given; rights talk is treated critically.

conscription.rationale: Inferred from nonviolence and critique of state violence.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Inferred from emphasis on collective assembly and participation.

state-as-business.rationale: Inferred from rejection of market logic in public life.

positive-liberty.rationale: Inferred from Butler's attention to material conditions of precarity.

media-academia-power.rationale: Adherents hold that knowledge reflects power, but the claim that universities and media outrank elected officials is not theirs.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Butler treats natural categories as discursively produced and denies fixed essences, applying to race as well as sex.

organic-representation.rationale: Inferred from rejection of fixed communal categories as political foundations.

total-state.rationale: Foucauldian suspicion of power over every area of life.

national-rebirth.rationale: Inferred from rejection of nationalism; Butler has called anti-gender movements neo-fascist.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Inferred from critique of sovereignty and state violence.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Inferred from rejection of personal hierarchical authority.

bound-labor.rationale: Inferred from commitment to equality and critique of domination.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: The SEP says continental feminists suspect truth claims mask power relations, a Foucauldian theme also central to the Wikipedia account of post-structural feminism.

universal-morality.rationale: The SEP lists post-structuralism among traditions that reject a neutral universal standpoint, and Butler challenges the presumed universality of the feminist subject.

single-common-good.rationale: Butler favours open coalitions in which unity is not assumed in advance, contrary to one common good worked out by reason.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Butler criticizes Israeli policy and some forms of Zionism and says Israel does not represent all Jews; not an adherent consensus.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Butler's critique of Israeli policy bears on return rights but she is also wary of citizenship by descent, so inference leaves it split.

revive-national-language.rationale: Language revival politics is not discussed; Cixous's interest in new forms of language concerns gender, not nations.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Inferred from valuing participation and equal social standing.

school-vouchers.rationale: Inferred from left egalitarian commitments; not discussed.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Inferred from support for economic-justice policy.

economic-freedom.rationale: Inferred: the market-liberal claim conflicts with Butler's critique of profiteering.

rule-by-example.rationale: Inferred from distrust of moral exemplars as norm-enforcers.

national-self-determination.rationale: Butler criticizes nationalism yet supports the dispossessed; adherents split.

force-without-un.rationale: Inferred from critique of state violence and the state of exception.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Rejects universal reason as neutral, but also is not a faith-based position; split.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Inferred from Butler's concern for the ungrievable and anti-exclusion stance.

class-collaboration.rationale: The theory does not address employer-worker relations, and Butler's support for redistribution is not a doctrine of class conflict.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Inferred: adherents challenge canon and norms but are not described as favouring destroying institutions.

dominated-front.rationale: Butler's anti-imperial sympathies are offset by suspicion of unifying identities; no stated view on a common front.

workers-nation.rationale: Inferred from rejection of fixed identity categories as bases of politics.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Gender Trouble denies that gender roles express a prior nature, and the Wikipedia overview describes identities as contingent and discursive, leaving no basis for legally distinct roles.

ban-interest.rationale: Usury law is outside the theory, and no principle of it points either way.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Butler stresses that law and exclusion produce the categories they claim to reflect and that race intersects with gender.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Foucauldian view sees power as diffuse and productive, not a class tool, but Butler is sympathetic to left critique; split.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Inferred from left egalitarian environmental sympathy; not discussed.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Inferred from rejection of normalising demands to fit a single identity.

elite-replacement.rationale: Butler calls anti-gender conspiracy movements neo-fascist; the conspiracy claim is contrary to the stance.

proportional-representation.rationale: Inferred from plural, coalitional politics and attention to excluded voices.

national-mission.rationale: Inferred from critique of exclusion and of sovereign violence.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Post-structural feminists analyse gendered power but Butler warns a universal, transhistorical patriarchy fails to account for cultural specificity, so agreement is qualified.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Not a theoretical claim; adherents are critical of power but not populist.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Inferred from rejection of norms that police bodies and reproduction.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Inferred from Butler's critique of state violence.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Inferred from support for economic justice and state protection of the vulnerable.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Contrary to anti-essentialism and to the critique of racial categories.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Butler argues for equal grievability of lives, though she also criticizes the universal subject before the law, so agreement is qualified.

socialism-one-country.rationale: A debate internal to Marxism-Leninism that post-structural feminism does not take up.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Inferred from Butler's critique of colonial and exclusionary state forms and of Zionism; not directly stated.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Anti-universalism and anti-exclusion pull in opposite directions; no stated view.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Inferred from opposition to coercive norm enforcement.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Inferred from opposition to religiously motivated legal norms.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Inferred from preference for secular public institutions.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Inferred from suspicion of state power.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Butler endorses assembly and popular power, though she criticises how consent subjects are produced.

trade-surplus.rationale: Mercantilist trade policy is not addressed by the theory or by its sources.

population-transfer.rationale: Inferred from rejection of exclusion and from Butler's attention to ungrievable populations.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Butler's nonviolence ethic supports the claim, but property-focused libertarian framing is foreign to the theory.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Inferred from emphasis on interdependence and rejection of struggle as natural law.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Butler is wary of state censorship but also condemns neo-fascist movements; split.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Critique of the power that produces subjects aligns with anti-domination, though the republican vocabulary is not hers.

separated-powers.rationale: Constitutional design is not addressed; Butler's critique of sovereign exception is compatible with checks but does not require them.

vanguard-party.rationale: Butler rejects pre-given unity and a leading subject, favouring open coalition.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Inferred from support for economic justice and concern with precarity.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Housing tenure policy is outside the theory's concerns.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Inferred from support for assembly and left politics.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Inferred from attributing precarity to social arrangements, not nature.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Butler argues unity should not be assumed and that exclusions in the name of unity are the problem.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Sortition is not discussed; adherents' valuing of participation does not settle it.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Butler explicitly criticizes the state of exception at Guantanamo.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: No source addresses price policy and nothing in the principles decides it.

party-controls-media.rationale: Inferred from Foucauldian suspicion of controlled knowledge and Butler's anti-censorship stance.

party-commands-army.rationale: Inferred from rejection of one-party rule.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Politician pay is not addressed by the theory or its sources.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Inferred from rejection of unity presumed in advance.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Butler criticizes sovereignty, but supranational bodies are not discussed.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Inferred from distrust of concentrated executive power.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Inferred from rejection of hierarchical religious authority.

clerical-rule.rationale: Inferred from rejection of foundational authority.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Butler opposes state violence but the theory takes no stance on revolutionary defeatism.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Butler's Excitable Speech criticizes state censorship, including MacKinnon's anti-pornography campaign.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Inferred from distrust of concentrated power.

recall-officials.rationale: Inferred from valuing participation and accountability.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Butler's critique of militarism leans against alliances, but military blocs are not discussed directly.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Inferred only from the theory's lack of any programme for housing; an extreme proposal outside its concerns.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Inferred from rejection of naturalised moral hierarchies.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: National reunification is not addressed, and its distrust of national identity offsets any sympathy.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Inferred: the theory is an academic one and does not accept anti-intellectual claims.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Butler warns that universal frameworks colonise non-Western cultures, supporting cultural parity, though she rejects fixed cultural essences.

death-penalty.rationale: Inferred from nonviolence ethic and critique of state violence.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Inferred from the aim of teaching gender as non-natural; not explicitly stated.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Inferred from opposition to foundational religious claims in public institutions.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Butler criticizes MacKinnon's anti-pornography stance for accepting state censorship.

minority-language-support.rationale: Inferred from attention to excluded voices.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Competing pulls: protection of minorities versus exemptions from equality law.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Butler urges subversive repetition and proliferation of gender and identities outside the norm.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Anti-colonial sympathies suggest assent but no source states this claim.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Assembly valued but no stance on constitutional process.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Inferred from opposition to curbs on assembly and expression.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Inferred from interdependence and equal grievability themes.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Inferred from nonviolence and critique of militarism.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Electoral design for the head of state is not discussed.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Monetary institutions are outside the theory's scope.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Butler criticizes Israeli policy; inferred rejection of historic-claim logic.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Inferred from critique of profiteering, though talk of one common good is resisted.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: A debate within Marxist history that the sources do not touch.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Environmental regulation is not discussed; no principle of the theory decides it.

collective-defense.rationale: Alliance obligations are not addressed; Butler's anti-militarism is offset by concern for protecting the vulnerable.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Inferred from Butler's critique of occupation in Israel and Palestine.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Anti-clerical but also wary of state power; split.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Ceremonial headship of state is not addressed.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Inferred from critique of state violence.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Special-autonomy arrangements are not discussed by the sources.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Inferred from rejection of naturalised authority.

character-from-environment.rationale: Butler holds that subjects are discursively and socially constituted rather than natural, extending to the formation of character and identity.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Butler's critique of sovereign exception opposes rulers standing above law.

space-expansion.rationale: Space policy is not addressed by the theory.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Classical constitutional theory is outside the field of the sources.

leader-cult.rationale: Inferred from distrust of authority and Butler's account of plural assembly.

equal-parenting.rationale: Anti-essentialism supports gender-neutral parenting, but no stated view on presumptions.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: A debate within Maoism that post-structural feminism does not take up.

refugee-return.rationale: Inferred from Butler's concern for the dispossessed and her critique of Israeli policy.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Contrary to critique of unity and exclusion built on ethnic identity.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Contrary to opposition to enforced norms.

women-must-cover.rationale: Contrary to critique of state-policed gender norms.

common-currency.rationale: Monetary union is not addressed by the sources.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Inferred from rejection of identity-based unity.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Minority self-government is not discussed; adherents' wariness of fixed identity and support for minorities leave it split.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Butler's views on Zionism lean this way, but the question is not addressed generally.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Post-structuralism stresses discourse and power over economic base.

ban-cartels.rationale: Inferred from critique of concentrated economic power.

no-bailouts.rationale: Inferred from critique of profiteers; bank bailouts contested.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Inferred: Butler treats minority protection as vital but critiques liberal juridical subject; leaning against majoritarian override.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Inferred from feminist commitment to women's inclusion; yet Butler cautions against fixed category of women, so qualified.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Inferred from rejection of exclusionary unity.

moral-incentives.rationale: A question of socialist economic management the theory does not take up.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Inferred from rejection of naturalised hierarchy.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Inferred from rejection of identity-centred unity and from the critique of Western universals presented as neutral.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Butler warns universal frameworks colonise non-Western cultures.

patriotic-education.rationale: Inferred from critique of identity-based unity.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Inferred from attention to exclusion; affirmative action not stated.

public-money-creation.rationale: Monetary reform is not addressed by the sources.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Crisis theory is not a concern of the theory, and its sources take no view.

delink-world-market.rationale: Development strategy is not discussed in the sources.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: A debate within Marxist political economy that the theory does not enter.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Butler's critique of exclusion makes licence to discriminate contrary to the theory.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Butler criticizes the juridical subject yet values legal protection; split.

elective-rulers.rationale: Inferred from rejection of hereditary rule.

minority-veto.rationale: Wariness of majority rule but absolute veto not discussed.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Butler's critique of the state of exception and defence of assembly implies a right to resist.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Parliamentary versus monarchic authority is not addressed.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Inferred from emphasis on vulnerability and grievability; animals not discussed.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Animal ethics is not covered by the sources, and no principle of the theory settles it.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Inferred from preferring structural equality to paternalistic duty.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Butler's work centres on political intervention and assembly.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Inferred from Foucault-influenced view that cultural discourse reproduces norms.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Post-structural accounts of power as operating through discourse and norms align with the claim that dominance works through culture as well as force.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Dependency theory is not part of this theory and the sources do not discuss it.

party-own-road.rationale: A question internal to communist parties that the theory does not address.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Inferred from critique of nationalist claims.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Support for indigenous claims but no stated view on political leadership.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Butler calls anti-gender movements neo-fascist, implying strong anti-fascism.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: The sources take no side on comparative judgements of fascism and communism.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Inferred from attention to race and power in history.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Inferred from attention to who is grievable and who is honoured.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Anti-essentialism neither endorses nor opposes; adherents split.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Inferred from gendered-power analysis, though not stated.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Warns against Western frameworks colonising other cultures but opposes cultural essences.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Inferred from critique of state violence.

paid-care-work.rationale: Inferred from feminist concern with the gendered devaluation of care labour; not stated in the cited sources.

filial-duty.rationale: Inferred from critique of norms that impose fixed family roles.

office-by-exam.rationale: Civil-service selection is not discussed in the sources.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Foreign investment policy is outside the theory's scope.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Inferred from rejection of norm-enforcing family law.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Delegate recall is not discussed; adherents' interest in participation does not decide it.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Inferred from support for social protection.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Land tenure systems are not addressed by the sources.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Fiscal procedure is not addressed by the sources.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Land-ownership rules for foreigners are not discussed.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Inferred from attention to how norms produce exclusion regardless of intent.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Inferred from critique of profiteering; not stated.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Inferred from critique of state violence and sovereign exception.

corporate-influence.rationale: Inferred from Butler's critique of profiteering and support for equality.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Inferred from support for civil society and assembly.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Inferred from rejection of state steering of reproduction.

democratic-peace.rationale: International relations theory is outside the sources' scope.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Butler defends civil disobedience-like assembly but no general theory of obligation.

non-intervention.rationale: Butler critiques interventionism but also advocates international protection of rights.

industrial-unions.rationale: Union structure is not discussed in the sources.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Butler condemns conspiracy-driven anti-gender movements as neo-fascist.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Butler writes on marriage and kinship critically, but source does not state a position and adherents differ.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Inferred from valuing open assembly and accountability.

local-production.rationale: Localism in production is not discussed in the sources.

informal-organisation.rationale: Butler's provisional coalitional politics resembles informal, non-permanent organisation.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Butler criticizes state sovereignty and exception, favouring wider protections.

religious-nation.rationale: Contrary to rejection of identity-based unity.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Property doctrine is not addressed by the sources.

defeat-communism.rationale: Inferred from left sympathies; not stated.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Public-service delivery models are not discussed.

religion-illusion.rationale: Not a Marxist claim in this theory; adherents split.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Inferred from critique of profiteering and precarity.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Butler's intersectional view links gender to class, but post-structural feminism centres discourse, so qualified.

socialized-care.rationale: Care labour valued but socialising it is not addressed.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Inferred from rejection of purity and boundary policing.

treaties-binding.rationale: Treaty law with internal nations is not addressed, though anti-colonial sympathies hint at support.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Communal property is not discussed by the sources.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Third-way economics is not discussed by the sources.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Butler criticizes claims based on historic tie in Israel and Palestine; inferred general rejection.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Butler's grievability framework and anti-fascist stance entail rejection; she is Jewish and writes on Jewish ethics.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: The Wikipedia overview says the approach criticizes heteronormativity and the exclusion of homosexual subjects, and Gender Trouble builds its critique on denaturalising compulsory heterosexuality.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Butler defends assembly and opposes state censorship.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Butler opposes state censorship of expression.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: A matter of Islamic jurisprudence outside the theory.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Inferred from opposition to foundational religious authority.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Butler analyses assembly as performative power and supports Occupy-style popular participation.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Gender Trouble notes gender intersects with race, class, ethnicity and sexuality and cannot be separated from them, though the theory's frame is discursive rather than structural.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Butler warns against anti-gender movements targeting trans and nonbinary people and the Wikipedia overview names transgender subjects among those excluded by heteronormativity.

assisted-dying.rationale: Inferred from emphasis on bodily autonomy; not discussed.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Butler is firmly on the left in positions on equality and economic justice.

alienated-labor.rationale: The sources do not take up Marx's concept of alienation.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Butler warns universal frameworks colonise non-Western cultures; opposes essentialising claims.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Inferred from rejection of foundational authority.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Conflicting pulls: anti-essentialism versus anti-policing of bodies; split.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Inferred from feminist concern for victims of harassment; specific policy not stated.

social-market-economy.rationale: Economic-order models are not discussed by the sources.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Great-power alignment is not addressed by the sources.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Inferred from rejection of naturalised hereditary hierarchy.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Mutualist banking is not discussed by the sources.

property-franchise.rationale: Inferred from support for equality and inclusion.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Post-structural feminists criticize naturalising women, a different move from ecofeminist linkage; split.

reification.rationale: The sources do not take up Lukacs's concept, though Foucauldian talk of produced subjects is loosely related.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Inferred from critique of profiteering and attention to who controls discourse.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Butler criticizes the juridical subject but values legal protection.

racial-franchise.rationale: Contrary to critique of exclusion and racial categories.

online-participation.rationale: Inferred from valuing participation and assembly.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Inferred from opposition to norm-enforcing marriage law.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Contrary to anti-exclusion stance and condemnation of neo-fascist targeting.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Inferred from valuing popular assembly and deliberation.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Inferred from favouring reinterpretation of fixed norms.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Inferred from opposition to exclusion of sexual minorities; though some adherents criticise the military.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Inferred from opposition to state-enforced norms.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Inferred from critique of state violence and Foucault-inspired suspicion of carceral power.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Consociational design is not discussed by the sources.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Inferred from support for state protection of the vulnerable.

term-limits.rationale: Office-holding rules are outside the theory's scope.

vote-delegation.rationale: Liquid democracy is not discussed by the sources.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Longtermist policy is not addressed by the theory.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Inferred from feminist opposition to gendered exclusion.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Inferred from rejection of gender hierarchy in marriage.

abolish-ip.rationale: Intellectual property is not discussed in the sources.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Inferred from Foucauldian critique of disciplinary power.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Butler's work on grievable lives supports recognising mass killings.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Butler's nonviolence is political ethic, not absolute pacifism, as the Wikipedia article stresses it is not passivity.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Gender Trouble questions whether sex is itself culturally constructed and says the sex/gender distinction may be none at all; the SEP cites Butler for the continental view that sex is socially constituted.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Butler argues that the presumed unity of the category of women is produced by the juridical systems meant to represent it and that feminist politics may make sense only when the subject of 'women' is nowhere presumed.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Inferred from critique of militarised nationalism.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Inferred from rejection of foundational moral metaphysics.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Diaspora nationalism is not addressed, and distrust of identity foundations offsets any sympathy.

culture-before-state.rationale: The sequencing of national cultural and political projects is not discussed.

god-not-male.rationale: Irigaray and Cixous criticize phallocentric symbolic orders; inferred extension to religious language.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Adherents may sympathise with the feminist critique of religious texts, but the theory itself is not a theology and the sources do not say.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Administrative border questions are not addressed by the sources.

independent-unions.rationale: Inferred from valuing autonomous collective action.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: A debate within Marxism that the theory does not enter.

second-chamber.rationale: Legislative structure is not discussed by the sources.

municipal-property.rationale: Municipalist property forms are not discussed in the sources.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Libertarian municipalism is not discussed in the sources.

family-wage.rationale: The male-breadwinner family wage assumes distinct gender roles that the approach denaturalises; also feminists generally criticise it.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Medical regulation is not addressed in the sources.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Research funding priorities are not addressed in the sources.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Surveillance suspicion but no stated position on payments.

online-anonymity.rationale: Inferred from the view that identity is performed and mutable, and from suspicion of surveillance.

person-over-state.rationale: Butler criticizes the sovereign juridical subject but also state violence against persons.

spiritual-nature.rationale: The sources do not address spirituality, and the theory's anti-foundationalism offsets Irigaray's interest in the sacred.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Devolution terms are not addressed by the sources.

gm-crops.rationale: Agricultural biotechnology is not addressed in the sources.

dense-cities.rationale: Urban planning is not addressed in the sources.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Butler's coalitional politics treats identities as provisionally taken up, not fixed group interests.

racial-pride.rationale: Inferred from rejection of essentialist race identity; not stated.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Inferred from rejection of fixed identity as basis of politics.

communal-electorates.rationale: Inferred from rejection of fixed identity categories as political foundations.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Inferred from rejection of conspiracy narratives.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Environmental taxation is not addressed in the sources.

future-generations.rationale: Intergenerational ethics is not addressed in the sources.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Post-structural feminists reject female essentialism, though Irigaray affirms sexual difference; most adherents deny innate distinct values.

capital-controls.rationale: Capital-account policy is not discussed in the sources.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Butler's critique of state violence offsets concern about armed groups, so no clear view follows.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Wage-subsidy design is not discussed in the sources.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Inferred from support for social spending.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Inferred from economic-justice and anti-colonial orientation.

smash-state-machine.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist question; Butler's critique of sovereign exception does not extend to a programme of overthrow.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Economic pluralism between communities is not discussed in the sources.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Inferred from critique of systems that turn things into commodities and from Butler's anti-capitalist writing; the sources do not discuss pricing nature.

sacred-nation.rationale: Inferred from the strand's view of collective identities as contingent products of discourse and power, which denies any natural or sacred standing to the nation.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Inferred from Butler's backing of economic-justice demands and concern for precarity; the sources give no education-finance doctrine.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Inferred from the strand's attention to how power and discourse subordinate groups, and from postcolonial overlap; not stated in the sources.

shared-human-nature.rationale: The strand treats sex, gender and identity as contingent products of discourse and rejects essentialism, so a fixed shared nature as the ground of dignity is doubtful; Butler does ground claims in shared vulnerability, hence low.

public-service-media.rationale: Inferred from the strand's critique of dominant discourses and its egalitarian politics; public media is not a topic in the sources.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Inferred from the rejection of universal essences and truth claims, which extends to a single underlying religious truth.

farm-price-support.rationale: Not a post-structural topic and no stated position; no lean can be inferred.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Inferred from Butler writings on nonviolence and critique of state violence.

workers-own-party.rationale: Butler backs economic-justice protest but the sources give no view on separate class parties; post-structuralism distrusts fixed class subjects.

ban-fgm.rationale: Adherents are split between concern for harm to women and suspicion of universalist, colonial framing of non-Western practices; no source settles it.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Inferred from the general commitment to equality, though the sources give no property doctrine and the category women is itself questioned.

one-language-many-names.rationale: No stated position; naming is treated as discursive and contingent, which points both ways.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Inferred from Butler wider left, anti-corporate politics, which favours public regulation over private suits.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Inferred from suspicion of authority and patriarchal institutions; the sources do not address chiefs.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Not addressed in the sources, and the strand stresses both precarious lives and resistance to state coercion.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Inferred from Butler critique of state power and the carceral state; sentencing is not discussed directly.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Inferred from the rejection of norm-enforcing, assimilationist demands; not directly addressed.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Not a post-structural topic; no stated stance, and the left-leaning milieu is split on compulsory dues.

voter-id.rationale: Inferred from Butler's concern for precarious, unequally protected groups, who tend to be hit hardest by ID requirements.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Inferred from the rejection of single authoritative readings and fixed truth claims, which opposes giving one interpretation legal precedence.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Inferred from Butler's view of politics as contestation over who counts as a subject, which asks for more than elections.

premarital-sex.rationale: Inferred from the critique of heteronormativity and of norms that regulate gendered sexuality; the sources do not discuss marriage directly.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Inferred from Butler's opposition to state control over speech and assembly and her concern for the vulnerable; not addressed in the sources.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Economic policy design is not addressed; the left-leaning milieu favours welfare but has no stated view on cash-transfer schemes.

women-suffrage.rationale: Inferred from its egalitarian politics; it criticises 'women' as a fixed category but does not question women's equal political rights.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Inferred: the strand treats oppression as produced by discourse in general, not mainly religion, and does not single religion out.

race-social-construct.rationale: Inferred from its view that identity categories such as sex are produced by discourse and power; race is not the strand's own focus.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Inferred: it distrusts institutionalising a fixed category of women, yet supports gender justice; adherents are split on state bodies.

missingStatements.text: Language and the symbolic order shape what can be thought, so changing how we write and speak is itself a form of political action.
missingStatements.rationale: Cixous's écriture féminine and Irigaray's call for a new symbolic order hold that disrupting patriarchal language is political.

missingStatements.text: Heterosexuality is a social norm that society enforces, not simply a natural fact.
missingStatements.rationale: The overview says Butler holds that 'normal' identities depend on rejecting deviant ones within heteronormativity.

notes: Irigaray affirms sexual difference while Butler questions it, and Cixous and Kristeva declined the feminist label. Most economic and institutional answers are inferred from Butler's wider left politics and are low confidence.
